variables.description: Variable values to substitute into the prompt template. Any JSON values allowed — strings, arrays, or objects. Caller decides the shape per variable. Objects and arrays are rendered as readable markdown into the prompt; the LLM reads whatever's provided. Multibrand is the default in this platform, so brand-related variables typically receive arrays or objects, not scalars. Per-template input expectations are published via GET /platform-prompts?type=<type> (.variables: Array<{ name, description }>), alongside .contextVariables: optional lead and organization inputs every template accepts (person, employment history, organization industries, funding, location, and more). One of them, leadRelationship, says who the recipient already is to the brand (relationship, thread, strategy): it is rendered as its own section and its strategy wins over a template written as a first contact. When values are string-typed, recognised keys may also populate dedicated dashboard columns: leadFirstName, leadLastName, leadTitle, leadCompanyName, leadCompanyIndustry, organizationDomain, clientCompanyName.

model.description: LLM model to generate with (version-free alias). Provider is derived automatically: anthropic → haiku | sonnet | opus; google → flash-lite | flash | flash-pro | pro; deepseek → deepseek-flash (DeepSeek V4 Flash) | deepseek-pro (DeepSeek V4 Pro); zai → glm-flash (glm-4.7-flashx) | glm-pro (glm-5.2); moonshot → kimi-flash (kimi-k2.6) | kimi-pro (kimi-k3). The six deepseek/zai/moonshot aliases are called directly on each vendor's OpenAI-compatible API. That path is text-only, which this service never exceeds; note that JSON-mode enforcement there is best-effort (fails loud rather than degrading), and a vendor whose account is out of credit answers 429 — surfaced as an error naming the provider, never silently rerouted to another vendor. Omit to use the default 'pro' (google) — unchanged from before this field existed. Every alias stays accepted here whatever its staff status: a NEW workflow must not name one whose status is `deprecated` on GET /internal/models, but a stored workflow that does keeps generating.

post.summary: Write ONE cold email for a brand and a sample recipient, before any campaign exists
post.description: Writes the email the visitor would receive once they pay: the prompt template AND model of the fleet's best MATURE cold-email workflow (features-service leg ranking, read at request time, cached a few minutes), with that workflow's own brand intel request and input mapping. 502/503 when the ranking or the workflow cannot be read: there is no fallback template or model. A request carrying `model` is refused (400). The LLM spend is declared and authorized against the calling org by chat-service; an org that cannot afford it gets 402. Creates no campaign, no lead and no email_generations row, so nothing here can be sent or counted. The same brand + recipient (+ audience, offer, model) returns the stored email instead of a second billed completion, as long as the best workflow is unchanged.

post.summary: Get ready to write preview emails for a brand (fire and forget)
post.description: Sends brand-service, in the background, the same brand-intel request POST /preview-email will send for this brand (the best mature workflow's own field set), so the first preview finds it cached and only pays for the model. Answers 202 at once and never waits for the site read (which can take minutes). Idempotent: at most one warm-up per org + brand runs at a time, a repeat while it runs or shortly after it completes starts nothing, and brand-service's field cache makes any later repeat a cache read. A POST /preview-email arriving while a warm-up runs waits for it rather than reading the site a second time. Billing: the only spend is that brand-service read, the preview's own spend moved earlier, billed by brand-service to the calling org (x-org-id). No email is written and no completion is made here.

202.description: Warm-up started, already running, or recently completed

400.description: Invalid request or missing identity headers

Without `limit`, a result set over 2000 rows is refused with 413 rather than trimmed, so a partial list can never be mistaken for the whole one.

get.summary: Cascade example emails for a workflow (brand → org → global)
get.description: Returns up to `limit` content-bearing example emails for a workflow, with a fallback cascade so it (almost) always returns `limit`: (1) the caller's current brand, then (2) the caller's other brands, then (3) any org (examples are public). Each example is tagged with `scope` (which tier it came from) and `brandName` (the source brand's label for org/global tiers; null for own-brand). Brand-tier rows come first, newest-first within each tier. Content-less / failed generations are skipped. Default limit 3.

post.summary: Start rendering the daily industry debrief news-bulletin video (async)
post.description: Queues a render of the 4:5 news bulletin defined by the industry-debrief-video skill: per story the headline, the real post captured from its public embed with the sentence spotlit under a header saying who wrote it, why it matters + its note, what we think; reading time per screen from word count; house chrome; sign-off; music longer than the video (rotating Mixkit tracks, never looped). Answers 202 at once: a render takes several minutes, poll `GET /industry-debrief-videos/{id}?waitSeconds=240`. Renders run one at a time on the service's own CPU (no metered vendor); the R2 upload is declared by cloudflare-service on this run.

202.description: Queued (or the existing render for this idempotencyKey)

get.summary: A debrief render's status; optionally wait for it to finish
get.description: With `waitSeconds` (1-240) the call holds until the render is `done`/`failed` or the wait elapses, then answers the current state (always 200): one call stays under the platform's 300 s client timeout. A workflow polls it with `validateResponse: { field: "status", equals: "done" }` and retries.
